chapterNote: The 'Joy to the World' psalm — Isaac Watts's hymn is a paraphrase of it, and the church has sung it at Christmas because it is about the King arriving. It is Psalm 96's twin: sing a new song, for He has done wonders. But here the victory is already won — His right hand and holy arm have done it, unassisted — and already public: the LORD has unveiled His righteousness before the nations' eyes, and all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God, because He remembered His covenant love and faithfulness to Israel. Mary and Simeon both echo it. Then the orchestra assembles by sections: the whole earth shouting, lyre and voice, silver trumpets and ram's horn, then the sea thundering its bass line, the rivers clapping, the mountains singing in unison — and the reason for all the noise is the last line: He is coming to judge the earth with righteousness and the peoples with fairness. In the Psalms, judgment is what the oppressed have been waiting for; creation applauds because the Judge is good.

1.text: A psalm. Sing a new song to the LORD, for He has done wonders; His right hand and His holy arm have won Him the victory.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor]. O sing [shir] unto the LORD [YHWH] a new [chadash] song [shir]; for He has done [asah] marvellous things [pala — wonders beyond human ability]: His right hand [yamin], and His holy [qodesh] arm [zeroa], has gotten Him the victory [yasha — worked salvation].
1.notes: shir chadash (H7892, H2319): every fresh act of God demands fresh music. niphlaot (H6381), wonders past human reach — and the Victor is unassisted: yamin and zeroa qodsho (H3225, H2220, H6944), His own right hand and holy arm, yasha (H3467) for Him. Isaac Watts read this psalm and wrote 'Joy to the World'.

2.text: The LORD has made His salvation known; He has unveiled His righteousness before the eyes of the nations.
2.amp: The LORD [YHWH] has made known [yada] His salvation [yeshuah]: His righteousness [tsedaqah] has He openly showed ['revealed', galah — uncovered, the KJV margin] in the sight [ayin] of the heathen [goy].
2.notes: galah (H1540), the uncovering-verb — salvation not done in a corner but stripped of its veil le-ene ha-goyim (H5869, H1471), in the nations' eyes. Paul's gospel-thesis has this grammar: in it the tsedaqah (H6666) of God is revealed (cf. Romans 1:17).

3.text: He has kept in mind His covenant love and faithfulness toward Israel's house; the farthest reaches of the earth have all seen the saving work of our God.
3.amp: He has remembered [zakar] His mercy [chesed — covenant love] and His truth [emunah — faithfulness] toward the house [bayith] of Israel [Yisrael]: all the ends [ephes] of the earth [eretz] have seen [raah] the salvation [yeshuah] of our God [Elohim].
3.notes: Particular and universal in one breath: chesed and emunah (H2617, H530) zakar (H2142) for bet Yisrael — and because God kept faith with one small people, kol aphse eretz (H657, H776) raah the rescue. Mary's Magnificat echoes the first half; Simeon's Nunc Dimittis the second (cf. Luke 1:54; 2:30-31).

4.text: Raise a shout to the LORD, all the earth; break out, sing for joy, and make music!
4.amp: Make a joyful noise [rua — shout] unto the LORD [YHWH], all the earth [eretz]: make a loud noise [patsach — break forth, burst out], and rejoice [ranan — ring out], and sing [zamar — make music] praise.
4.notes: Four noise-verbs stacked: rua, patsach, ranan, zamar (H7321, H6476, H7442, H2167) — shout, burst, ring, play — the whole eretz conscripted as orchestra. patsach is the verb of a dam breaking: praise that cannot be held back.

5.text: Make music to the LORD with the lyre — with the lyre and the sound of melody;
5.amp: Sing [zamar] unto the LORD [YHWH] with the harp [kinnor — lyre]; with the harp, and the voice [qol] of a psalm [zimrah — melody].
5.notes: The kinnor (H3658), David's instrument, named twice — and qol zimrah (H6963, H2172), the sound of melody: strings and voice together. The instruments enter in order: strings first, then the brass of verse 6.

6.text: with trumpets and the blast of the ram's horn, raise a shout before the King, the LORD!
6.amp: With trumpets [chatsotserah — the long silver trumpets] and sound [qol] of cornet [shophar — ram's horn] make a joyful noise [rua] before [panim] the LORD [YHWH], the King [melek].
6.notes: The chatsotserot (H2689) are the temple's hammered-silver trumpets of Numbers 10; the shophar (H7782) the ram's horn of Sinai and Jericho. Both are royal fanfare here — rua liphne ha-melek YHWH (H4428): a coronation blast for the King arriving.

7.text: Let the sea thunder, and everything that fills it; the world, and all who live in it.
7.amp: Let the sea [yam] roar [raam — thunder], and the fulness [melo — 'all it containeth', the KJV margin] thereof; the world [tebel], and they that dwell [yashab] therein.
7.notes: raam (H7481) is the thunder-verb — the yam and its melo (H3220, H4393) told to add the bass line. tebel (H8398) is the inhabited world; nature and its tenants sing the same anthem, as in Psalm 96:11.

8.text: Let the rivers clap their hands; let the mountains ring out with joy together
8.amp: Let the floods [nahar — rivers] clap [macha] their hands [kaph — palms]: let the hills [har] be joyful [ranan] together [yachad]
8.notes: neharot yimchau khaph (H5104, H4222, H3709): rivers applauding, palm on palm — the sound of water breaking on rock heard as ovation. The harim ranan yachad (H2022, H7442, H3162), the mountains a choir singing in unison, as Isaiah 55:12 also hears them.

9.text: before the LORD, for He is on His way to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness, and the peoples with straight dealing.
9.amp: Before [panim] the LORD [YHWH]; for He comes [bo] to judge [shaphat] the earth [eretz]: with righteousness [tsedek] shall He judge [shaphat] the world [tebel], and the people [am] with equity [meyshar — straightness, fairness].
9.notes: The reason creation cheers: ki ba, He is coming — bo (H935) — lishpot (H8199). Judgment is good news in the Psalms because the Judge is tsedek and mesharim (H6664, H4339), straight dealing at last for every am (H5971). 'He comes to make His blessings flow far as the curse is found' — Watts got the verse exactly.
